# Parkinson's disease — facts

> Source-anchored research on Parkinson's disease: treatments, current and frontier research, adjunct therapies and lifestyle changes. Educational reference, not medical advice. Every line carries the URL it came from after the dash; optional `keywords:` and `also:` fields follow it, and `also:` lists sources that say the same thing.

## Parkinson's disease motor drug therapy: levodopa, dopamine agonists, MAO-B/COMT/A2A drugs, fluctuations, dyskinesia, gait and medication safety
<a id="parkinson-s-disease-motor-drug-therapy-levodopa-dopamine-agonists-mao-b-comt-a2a-drugs-fluctuations-dyskinesia-gait-and-medication-safety"></a>

- [statement] In a double-blind, randomized, controlled, crossover study (Neurology 2017) of single-dose intake in eighteen patients with advanced Parkinson disease, Mucuna pruriens (MP) powder from roasted seeds at a high dose containing 17.5 mg/kg of levodopa induced greater motor improvement at 90 and 180 minutes, longer ON duration and fewer dyskinesias than dispersible levodopa plus benserazide (3.5 mg/kg), and the authors concluded that single-dose MP met all noninferiority efficacy and safety outcome measures; a 2025 systematic review likewise states that this trial found MP significantly reduced dyskinesia at both 90 and 180 min compared to levodopa plus a decarboxylase inhibitor. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5539737/
- [statement] Both US apomorphine labels contraindicate concomitant use with ondansetron, listed among serotonin receptor antagonists, because profound hypotension and loss of consciousness have been reported. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine, PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety · also: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=3235535d-9ef9-4657-8b2a-176a807d091c
- [statement] For early PD, the AAN review found greater motor improvement with initial levodopa than with initial dopamine agonists, while initial agonists caused less dyskinesia during the first five years; severe or disabling dyskinesia was uncommon in that interval. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] ONAPGO prescribing information revised May 2026 describes subcutaneous infusion for motor fluctuations in adults with advanced PD; it explicitly states that ONAPGO is not substitutable for apomorphine products intended for intermittent use. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma announced on October 23, 2025 that the US FDA had issued a complete response letter for the new drug application of investigational ND0612 for motor fluctuations in people with Parkinson's disease, with FDA observations regarding the manufacturing site and the nonclinical information. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-23) — https://www.tanabe-pharma.com/en/news/news20251023103060.html · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] COMT inhibition reduces levodopa conversion to 3-O-methyldopa and increases levodopa availability; it is an adjunct mechanism that depends on levodopa treatment. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide and opicapone can cause or worsen dyskinesia when added to levodopa; both US labels state that reducing levodopa or another dopaminergic drug may mitigate it. (medium confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Istradefylline is an adenosine A2A receptor antagonist used in the US label as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa for adult OFF episodes; its precise therapeutic mechanism is unknown. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=a7d008cb-b273-4049-a5d2-9c6902910d58&type=pdf · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The US XADAGO label uses safinamide as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa for OFF episodes: start at 50 mg once daily, with an increase to 100 mg once daily after two weeks according to need and tolerability; doses above 100 mg have no demonstrated added benefit. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Entacapone is given as 200 mg with each levodopa/decarboxylase-inhibitor dose; its short duration adds dosing burden, and reported adverse effects include diarrhea, urine discoloration and dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Selegiline and rasagiline can provide modest symptomatic benefit as monotherapy in early Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide adjunct trials support reduced OFF time and increased ON time without troublesome dyskinesia; the MDS review describes benefits around one hour compared with placebo, although individual trials vary. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Selegiline and rasagiline inhibit MAO-B irreversibly, whereas safinamide inhibits it reversibly. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide inhibits MAO-B and thereby reduces dopamine catabolism; additional effects on glutamate release and sodium channels have been described, but their added clinical relevance remains uncertain. (medium confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] The MDS review found insufficient evidence for selegiline specifically as treatment of motor fluctuations despite attempted optimal oral levodopa therapy, citing small samples, low-quality evidence and heterogeneous results; this conclusion is scoped to that indication. (low confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Opicapone has placebo-controlled evidence for reducing OFF time; the MDS review found no significant PDQ-39 improvement in its included trials. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Safinamide has drug-specific interaction restrictions: its US label contraindicates other MAO inhibitors, including linezolid, selected opioids such as tramadol, SNRIs and certain other antidepressants, and dextromethorphan; SSRIs instead require the lowest effective dose and monitoring for serotonin syndrome. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=c4d65f28-983f-42b4-bb23-023ae0fe81b2 · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Istradefylline’s non-dopaminergic receptor target does not eliminate dyskinesia or psychiatric adverse effects: the US label warns of worsened dyskinesia and hallucinations and advises against treatment in major psychotic disorders. (low confidence) — https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/getFile.cfm?setid=a7d008cb-b273-4049-a5d2-9c6902910d58&type=pdf · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] Motor fluctuations are transitions between ON, when levodopa provides useful symptomatic benefit, and OFF, when responsive symptoms re-emerge and function declines. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] NICE recommendation 1.3.9 advises seeking Parkinson’s specialist advice before modifying therapy when dyskinesia or motor fluctuations, including wearing-off, develop. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] NICE advises considering amantadine when dyskinesia is not adequately managed by modifying existing therapy; the Aradi–Hauser review likewise includes it among options for peak-dose dyskinesia. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] Wearing-off is gradual loss of dose benefit before the next dose; sudden OFF can be unrelated to dose timing, delayed ON means unusually slow benefit after a dose, and dose failure means no benefit from that dose. These are distinct response patterns. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] When dyskinesia and OFF coexist on immediate-release carbidopa–levodopa, smaller individual doses given more frequently (fractionation) may help reduce peak–trough fluctuations; this is an option rather than a guaranteed response. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] For fluctuations inadequately controlled by oral medication, infusion therapies can be considered; the MDS review supports selected continuous-delivery treatments as likely efficacious, rather than guaranteeing benefit for every patient. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] Peak-dose dyskinesia occurs at the peak of the levodopa response; diphasic dyskinesia occurs as levodopa levels rise and fall. Painful dystonia can also occur during OFF, particularly early morning OFF. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] A common initial strategy for wearing-off is to shorten the interval between levodopa doses. Practical schedule adjustments are widely used, but the 2025 MDS review notes that not all have been tested in randomized trials. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] For dyskinesia without OFF time, the Aradi–Hauser review suggests considering lower individual levodopa doses or reducing adjunctive medication. This recommendation is explicitly for that response pattern. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] If schedule adjustments do not sufficiently improve motor fluctuations, additional medical treatment may be needed; persistent inadequate control can prompt consideration of pump therapy or a neurosurgical procedure. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] NICE NG71 lists the person's individual clinical circumstances (for example symptoms, comorbidities and risks from polypharmacy), their lifestyle circumstances, preferences, needs and goals, and the potential benefits and harms of the different drug classes among its considerations in choosing treatment; the MDS review states that safety and individual tolerability must be taken into account together with each patient's preference. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] The 2025 MDS review explicitly states that its efficacy designations do not prioritize treatment order or establish larger benefit for an “efficacious” treatment than for a “likely efficacious” treatment. It also notes few long-term comparative studies to guide the first treatment choice. (low confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.30162 · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] The MDS review illustrates that OFF-time reduction does not necessarily translate into a clinically meaningful improvement in disability or quality of life: its extended-release levodopa comparison improved OFF/ON outcomes but did not reach clinical relevance for those broader outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12089898/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] The motor-complications review describes no significant difference in motor-complication rates at 80 weeks in a trial comparing immediate levodopa initiation with a 40-week delay; this finding does not establish that longer delays prevent complications. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7851275/ · keywords: Motor fluctuations, wearing-off and dyskinesia management
- [statement] A pharmacy-informatics review states that medications affecting dopaminergic states must be used cautiously in Parkinson's disease, and singles out dopamine antagonists in the antipsychotic class (including haloperidol) and the antiemetic class (including metoclopramide, promethazine and prochlorperazine) as able to worsen Parkinson motor function. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10682362/ · keywords: PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] NICE limits its discussion of protein redistribution to people taking levodopa who experience motor fluctuations, and specifically advises against reducing total daily protein intake. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] The 2020 caffeine meta-analysis reported a progression association from cohort endpoints such as dyskinesia, motor fluctuation and levodopa initiation, but explicitly noted that none of its included studies isolated pure caffeine tablets and that an optimal caffeine dose could not be defined. Its pooled progression association should not be treated as randomized evidence of disease modification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7353179/
- [statement] Protein redistribution requires nutritional and medication monitoring: the 2023 practical review advises avoiding low-protein diets below 0.8 g/kg/day to prevent lean-mass loss, monitoring weight and dyskinesias, and considering levodopa dose adjustment when bioavailability improves. Its minimum is not a universal optimal protein prescription. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-023-00541-w
- [statement] Dietary protein can reduce or delay levodopa effectiveness in some people with PD. Protein-related motor fluctuations are a reason to review meal timing and medication response with the treating team; nausea can make an empty-stomach regimen difficult, and a small carbohydrate snack may help. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/management/diet-nutrition
- [statement] PADOVA is a Phase 2b, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study in which individuals with early-stage PD on stable symptomatic monotherapy (levodopa or MAO-Bi) receive intravenous prasinezumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39798255/
- [statement] Roche reports that in a pre-specified analysis the effect of prasinezumab in PADOVA was more pronounced in the population treated with levodopa (75% of participants), with HR=0.79 and a nominal p=0.0431. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-06-16) — https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2024-12-19
- [statement] In PADOVA, the primary endpoint of time to confirmed motor progression was not met: Roche reports HR=0.84 and p=0.0657, and the Lancet paper reports a non-significant delay in motor progression with prasinezumab versus placebo. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-30) — https://www.roche.com/media/releases/med-cor-2024-12-19
- [statement] The REASON authors report adverse events in 64.5% (20/31) of part A participants and 84.8% (28/33) of part B participants, mainly mild to moderate and not dose limiting, with no serious adverse events related to BIIB094. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41876647/ · keywords: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
- [statement] NeurologyLive reports that treatment-emergent adverse events led to study drug withdrawal in 11.2% of BIIB122/DNL151-treated LUMA participants versus 4.6% of placebo-treated participants. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-05) — https://www.neurologylive.com/view/lrrk2-inhibitor-biib122-fails-slow-early-stage-parkinson-disease · keywords: LRRK2-targeted therapies: small molecule and antisense
- [statement] Two small randomised trials of reduced-dose LSVT BIG protocols differ in what they report: a trial of a 2-week short protocol with identical exercises found motor performance equally improved versus standard LSVT BIG, whereas a trial of a modified protocol (twice weekly in clinic and twice weekly at home) reported the standard protocol favoured on some balance and gait measures. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24872078/ · keywords: LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy
- [statement] Two analyses of commercial Mucuna pruriens products reported wide variation in levodopa content: a 2018 HPLC analysis of six products found levodopa content varying from 6% to 141% of label claims with no product within the 90%–110% pharmacopeial limits, and a 2022 JAMA Neurology case series of 16 analyzed supplements found 15 containing levodopa at 2 mg to 241 mg per recommended serving, with actual levodopa 228% to 2186% greater than the estimate for products listing a seed-extract quantity, while carbidopa and benserazide were not detected. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5808387/
- [statement] Sources differ on adverse events with Mucuna pruriens (MP) in Parkinson disease: a 2025 systematic review (5 clinical trials, 108 participants; one study rated high quality, one with some concerns and three low quality) found MP associated with fewer adverse events and no dyskinesia reported while calling current clinical evidence limited, whereas a 12-month open-label phase 2 randomized trial in thirty-two untreated patients reported more frequent adverse events with MP than with levodopa plus a decarboxylase inhibitor (56% vs. 37.5%, p = 0.48; not statistically significant) and stated that larger double-blind trials with extended follow-up of 24–36 months are needed. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12377966/
- [statement] When medication reduction is not anticipated and suppressing on-medication dyskinesia is the goal, the CNS guideline favors GPi; GPi can have a direct antidyskinetic effect while medication is maintained. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/
- [statement] Both STN and GPi are effective motor-symptom targets; the CNS guideline supports either target for motor treatment rather than a universal target preference. (medium confidence) — https://www.cns.org/guidelines/congress-of-neurological-surgeons-systematic-revie/
- [statement] Apomorphine pump continuation is a separate outcome from motor benefit: a retrospective 110-patient study reported 35% discontinuation over two years and stable quality of life among continuers despite sustained motor-fluctuation reduction; another 208-patient cohort found that many discontinuations were switches to DBS, so discontinuation is not synonymous with drug failure. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-021-00194-7 · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] FDA's Drugs@FDA record for NDA 216962 lists the original approval of Vyalev (foscarbidopa and foslevodopa) injection on 10/16/2024; the FDA approval letter states that the NDA provides for subcutaneous use for the treatment of motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson's disease and acknowledges an August 16, 2024 amendment that constituted a complete response to FDA's June 18, 2024 action letter. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=216962 · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS, Regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) for PD therapies · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2024/216962Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- [statement] FDA's Drugs@FDA record for NDA 214056 lists the original approval of Onapgo (apomorphine hydrochloride) injection on 02/03/2025; the FDA approval letter states that the NDA provides for the treatment of motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson's disease and acknowledges an August 1, 2024 amendment that constituted a complete response to FDA's April 5, 2024 action letter. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/index.cfm?event=overview.process&ApplNo=214056 · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS, Regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) for PD therapies · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2025/214056Orig1s000ltr.pdf
- [statement] The European Medicines Agency's Onerji page states that Onerji (levodopa/carbidopa) received a marketing authorisation valid throughout the EU on 27 April 2026, for motor fluctuations in patients with advanced Parkinson's disease that are not sufficiently controlled by oral anti-Parkinson medicinal products; the manufacturer's announcement identifies Onerji as project code ND0612, a continuous subcutaneous infusion of liquid levodopa/carbidopa. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/onerji · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS, Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery · also: https://www.neuroderm.com/our-company/news-and-events/eu-marketing-authorization-for-onerji/
- [statement] In the 12-week active-controlled phase 3 foslevodopa-foscarbidopa trial, the incremental gain in ON time without troublesome dyskinesia versus oral immediate-release levodopa-carbidopa was 1·75 h; the incremental OFF-time reduction was 1·79 h. This was a comparison with oral therapy, not DBS or intestinal infusion. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36402160/ · keywords: Device-aided therapies compared: pumps, infusions and DBS
- [statement] Part III examination instructions require recording medication status, time since the last levodopa dose, and clinical ON/OFF state; these conditions matter when interpreting repeated motor examinations. (medium confidence) — https://www.movementdisorders.org/MDS-Files1/PDFs/Rating-Scales/MDS-UPDRS_English_FINAL.pdf · keywords: Clinical rating scales and outcome measures: MDS-UPDRS
- [statement] DAT-SPECT interpretation requires checking potentially interfering drugs and structural imaging: cocaine, amphetamines and methylphenidate can markedly reduce tracer binding, while anatomic lesions and atrophy can alter apparent striatal binding or shape. Medication changes require clinician-directed preparation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7300075/ · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] The FDA prescribing information for DATSCAN (ioflupane I 123 injection), revised 11/2022, indicates it as an adjunct to other diagnostic evaluations for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain imaging in adult patients with suspected parkinsonian syndromes or suspected dementia with Lewy bodies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2022/022454s010lbl.pdf · keywords: Imaging biomarkers: DaTscan, MRI and PET
- [statement] MDS bradykinesia requires slowness plus decrement in amplitude or speed, or progressive hesitations/halts, during continued movement; limb bradykinesia must be documented. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Supportive MDS features include a clear and dramatic dopaminergic treatment response, levodopa-induced dyskinesia, and clinically documented limb rest tremor; merely some improvement on treatment does not satisfy the dramatic-response criterion. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Medication review is central to differential diagnosis: drug-induced parkinsonism can be symmetric but can also closely mimic PD; symptoms often resolve after withdrawal, while continued progression can reflect underlying PD unmasked by the drug. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Amantadine is a weak uncompetitive NMDA-receptor antagonist; the Gocovri label states that its therapeutic mechanism is unknown and distinguishes anticholinergic-like adverse effects from demonstrated direct anticholinergic activity. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns against abrupt withdrawal because of worsening parkinsonism and neuropsychiatric symptoms; for treatment longer than 4 weeks it advises, if possible, halving the dose for the final week. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The 2003 Cochrane amantadine review found insufficient evidence for efficacy and safety for general idiopathic Parkinson symptoms from older trials; its searches extended through 2001, so that conclusion does not include the 2017 EASE LID dyskinesia trial. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8715353/ · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label indicates this extended-release amantadine product for dyskinesia during levodopa-based treatment and as adjunctive treatment for off episodes; these are product-specific indications. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The February 2026 Gocovri label warns that concomitant drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate anticholinergic-like adverse effects; it advises reducing the anticholinergic drug or Gocovri dose if atropine-like effects appear. (low confidence) — https://www.gocovrihcp.com/Gocovri_Digital_PI_MG.pdf · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] Benztropine and trihexyphenidyl are anticholinergic options used particularly in younger patients; cognitive impairment, confusion, hallucinations, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and urinary retention restrict their usefulness, especially with advancing age. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The Parkinson Foundation describes anticholinergics as predominantly useful for tremor with little effect on other symptoms; the Cochrane review found motor benefit over placebo but conflicting results and insufficient support for a preferential effect on tremor. The latter limits claims of established symptom selectivity. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/anticholinergic-drugs · keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
- [statement] The AAN recommends using the lowest effective dopamine-agonist dose and, when stopping treatment because of adverse effects, gradual dose reduction when possible with monitoring for dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Apomorphine infusion has specific local tolerability burdens: the ONAPGO label warns of infusion-site reactions and infections and instructs daily site changes; it also warns that treatment can cause or worsen dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] The 2021 AAN guideline allows dopamine agonists as initial treatment in selected early-PD patients younger than 60 years who are at higher dyskinesia risk; it advises against their use for initial treatment in those older than 70 years or with preexisting cognitive impairment, excessive daytime sleepiness, or hallucinations. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] The AAN found no strong evidence favoring ropinirole over pramipexole or extended-release over immediate-release pramipexole for early-PD motor efficacy; formulation, administration route, cost, and patient preferences should guide selection. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Dopamine agonists require monitoring for daytime somnolence, sudden sleep onset, hallucinations, nausea, and orthostatic hypotension; these are also explicit apomorphine-label safety concerns. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] APOKYN prescribing information revised January 2025 describes subcutaneous apomorphine for acute, intermittent treatment of OFF episodes in advanced PD and requires the first dose under medical supervision. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/021264s025lbl.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome can complicate tapering, with anxiety, panic, depression or dysphoria, fatigue and pain; symptoms may be refractory to levodopa replacement. Its recognition matters because it can prevent successful agonist withdrawal. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5077247/ · keywords: Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation
- [statement] Dopamine agonist exposure is a major ICD risk factor, but ICDs can occur with other dopaminergic therapies; absence of agonist treatment does not eliminate risk. (medium confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation
- [statement] A 2024 clinical review distinguishes DDS management from usual ICD management: DDS may require reducing levodopa or fast-acting apomorphine exposure, with monitoring for motor deterioration and withdrawal and sometimes inpatient multidisciplinary care. This is review guidance, not evidence of a proven universally effective regimen. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11098885/ · keywords: Impulse control disorders and dopamine dysregulation
- [statement] Rytary is an oral extended-release carbidopa-levodopa capsule; its beads dissolve and are absorbed at different rates. (medium confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] CREXONT contains immediate-release carbidopa/levodopa granules and extended-release levodopa pellets, combining rapid and sustained delivery within an oral capsule. (high confidence) — https://crexont.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/CREXONT-Full-Prescribing-Information-August-2024.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Intestinal levodopa infusion adds procedure and device burdens: DUOPA labeling warns that gastrointestinal procedure-related complications can require surgery or cause death. (low confidence) — https://www.rxabbvie.com/pdf/duopa_pi.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] DUOPA is carbidopa-levodopa enteral suspension delivered into the jejunum through a PEG-J tube and pump. Its March 2026 label specifies a 16-hour daily infusion, up to 2000 mg levodopa, followed by nighttime oral immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa. (low confidence) — https://www.rxabbvie.com/pdf/duopa_pi.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] The October 2024 VYALEV label permits infusion during waking hours or for 24 hours, with individualized infusion rates; the maximum recommended daily foslevodopa dose is 3,525 mg, approximately equivalent to 2,500 mg levodopa. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/216962s000lbl.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Foscarbidopa and foslevodopa are prodrugs converted in vivo to carbidopa and levodopa. The October 2024 VYALEV label indicates subcutaneous pump infusion for motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson’s disease. (high confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/216962s000lbl.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Conversion from immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa to CREXONT is not a 1:1 dose substitution; use formulation-specific conversion and titration rather than matching milligrams. (high confidence) — https://crexont.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/CREXONT-Full-Prescribing-Information-August-2024.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] In RISE-PD, 506 participants were randomized; IPX203 increased daily good ON time by a least-squares mean 0.53 hours versus immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa (95% CI 0.09–0.97), with mean dosing approximately three versus five times daily. Good ON meant ON without troublesome dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425876/ · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] RISE-PD compared IPX203 with immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa in patients already experiencing fluctuations. It did not establish efficacy in early PD versus placebo or prevention of later motor complications; protocol dosing was limited to no more often than every 6 hours. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10425876/ · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Inhaled levodopa (INBRIJA) is an intermittent treatment for OFF episodes in patients already treated with carbidopa/levodopa, rather than a stand-alone maintenance formulation. (high confidence) — https://www.inbrija.com/prescribing-information.pdf · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] In the foslevodopa-foscarbidopa phase 3 trial, continuous subcutaneous infusion improved ON time without troublesome dyskinesia and reduced OFF time compared with oral immediate-release levodopa-carbidopa, but infusion-site events were frequent and more participants discontinued treatment because of adverse events. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36402160/ · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Levodopa is converted to dopamine in the brain. Carbidopa inhibits peripheral levodopa decarboxylation, increasing levodopa availability to the brain and reducing peripheral nausea and vomiting; it does not remove central levodopa adverse effects. (high confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Oral carbidopa-levodopa is supplied as immediate-release tablets, controlled-release tablets, and extended-release capsules; the Parkinson’s Foundation describes Rytary as containing beads absorbed at different rates. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/prescription-medications/levodopa · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] BouNDless studied ND0612 as continuous subcutaneous levodopa-carbidopa solution, with supplemental oral levodopa-carbidopa if needed; its randomized phase followed open-label optimization of both regimens. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38499015/ · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] BouNDless reported more ON time without troublesome dyskinesia with ND0612 than with oral levodopa-carbidopa, while infusion-site reactions were its most common adverse events; the study findings should not be treated as a statement of regulatory approval. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38499015/ · keywords: Levodopa and carbidopa formulations and delivery
- [statement] Entacapone and opicapone act peripherally, while tolcapone crosses the blood–brain barrier and inhibits COMT centrally as well as peripherally. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10199833/ · keywords: MAO-B, COMT inhibitors and adenosine A2A antagonists
- [statement] NICE advises against abrupt withdrawal or sudden failure of antiparkinsonian treatment from poor absorption because of the risk of acute akinesia or neuroleptic malignant syndrome; drug holidays should not be used. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] A pharmacy workflow review recommends treating levodopa as time-critical, documenting administration times and reasons for deviations, and using overdue alerts and custom order times. Its proposed 30-minute window is an operational recommendation, not proof that every patient can safely tolerate that delay. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10682362/ · keywords: PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] The Foundation hospital checklist warns about mixing MAO-B inhibitors with listed pain medicines and calls for consultation among the Parkinson clinician, surgeon and anesthesiologist; this checklist does not establish identical interaction risks for every listed agent. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/sites/default/files/documents/safe-contraindicated-medications-2026.pdf · keywords: PD medication timing, interactions and hospital safety
- [statement] Levodopa is the principal pharmacological approach for troublesome Parkinsonian tremor; it can improve both resting and action tremor, although individual response varies. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041452/ · keywords: Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management
- [statement] The tremor review states that underdosing of levodopa or non-adherence are important causes of poor tremor control in clinical practice, and that impaired swallowing, altered gastric motility and bacterial overgrowth leading to impaired levodopa absorption may contribute to levodopa pseudoresistance. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041452/ · keywords: Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management
- [statement] For residual tremor, anticholinergics have only a restricted role in young cognitively intact patients, propranolol has limited supporting evidence, and clozapine may help but requires specialist safety monitoring because of serious adverse effects. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10041452/ · keywords: Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management
- [statement] ReSPonD was a phase 2 trial in people with Parkinson disease who had fallen, could walk unaided and did not have dementia: rivastigmine improved step-time variability during normal walking and a simple dual task, but not the complex dual task, and caused more gastrointestinal adverse effects. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26795874/ · keywords: Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management
- [statement] In the Espay randomized crossover trial, methylphenidate did not improve gait and tended to worsen motor function, sleepiness and quality of life; this negative trial limits extrapolation from positive open-label observations. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3068005/ · keywords: Tremor, gait, freezing and postural instability management
- [statement] NINDS states that levodopa may improve motor function in some people with MSA, although benefits are often short-lived. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/multiple-system-atrophy · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] NINDS describes dopamine produced by substantia nigra neurons as a chemical messenger supporting smooth, purposeful movements. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/parkinsons-disease · keywords: Basal ganglia circuitry and dopamine neurobiology
- [statement] The Parkinson’s Foundation states that medications, toxins or other neurological conditions can cause secondary parkinsonism. (low confidence) — https://www.parkinson.org/understanding-parkinsons/what-is-parkinsons/types-parkinsonisms · keywords: Movement disorders and neurodegeneration landscape
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated droxidopa efficacious only in the short term and possibly useful, while rating the PD-specific efficacy evidence for midodrine and fludrocortisone insufficient; prescribing recommendations should not be mistaken for strong long-term PD trial evidence. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] Antimuscarinic treatment for overactive bladder in PD requires attention to worsening constipation and cognitive adverse effects; the MAESTRO investigators describe these as reasons to study alternatives. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9682970/
- [statement] The 2004 PD dementia trial reported nausea in 29.0 percent versus 11.2 percent, vomiting in 16.6 percent versus 1.7 percent, and tremor in 10.2 percent versus 3.9 percent with rivastigmine versus placebo, respectively. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] Rivastigmine offers modest symptomatic cognitive benefit in Parkinson’s disease dementia. In the 24-week placebo-controlled trial, mean ADAS-cog improved by 2.1 points with rivastigmine versus a 0.7-point worsening with placebo; this trial result does not establish prevention of dementia progression. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15590953/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] Rivastigmine has the strongest established drug evidence for PD dementia: the 2019 MDS review rates it efficacious and clinically useful, and the 2024 German guideline recommends its use. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review classifies rivastigmine for nondementia cognitive impairment as investigational with insufficient evidence; the 2024 German guideline recommends against rivastigmine, donepezil, galantamine and memantine for PD-MCI. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] Galantamine recommendations also differ by guideline and date: the 2019 MDS review calls it possibly useful despite insufficient PD dementia efficacy evidence; the 2024 German guideline recommends against its use. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] Dementia drug evidence should not be extrapolated to PD-MCI. The 2024 German guideline recommends against rivastigmine, donepezil, galantamine and memantine for PD-MCI; the 2021 review likewise found no effective pharmacologic treatment for PD-MCI. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] The 2024 German guideline recommends rivastigmine for PDD and says donepezil might be used off label; it does not regard all cholinesterase inhibitors as equally supported. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11561078/ · keywords: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
- [statement] NICE recommends considering medication for drooling when non-drug management is unavailable or ineffective, considering glycopyrronium bromide and specialist referral for botulinum toxin A. It restricts other anticholinergics to people judged at minimal cognitive-adverse-effect risk. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] Dopaminergic medication does not reliably normalize swallowing: the management review states that swallowing does not necessarily improve, while the dysphagia consensus describes antiparkinsonian drug effects as controversial. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6995701/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] Botulinum toxin A and B have treatment evidence for PD drooling: the 2019 MDS review rated both efficacious and clinically useful with specialized monitoring, while SIAXI demonstrated benefit of incobotulinumtoxinA in a mixed neurological population that included PD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated venlafaxine clinically useful for PD depressive symptoms, but retained insufficient-evidence efficacy ratings for the reviewed SSRIs because PD-specific results were conflicting or limited; possibly useful reflected additional evidence outside PD. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] In the six-week phase 3 pimavanserin trial, SAPS-PD improved more than with placebo without observed motor worsening; adverse-event discontinuations were more frequent with pimavanserin, so the trial does not establish risk-free treatment. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24183563/
- [statement] Venlafaxine XR reduced depressive symptoms versus placebo in the 12-week SAD-PD trial without worsening motor function; the 2019 MDS review rates venlafaxine clinically useful for PD depressive symptoms. This establishes trial and review findings, not comparative superiority over all antidepressants. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3324323/
- [statement] Apathy drug evidence is restricted: the 2019 MDS review based rivastigmine possibly-useful status on one small positive study, and piribedil possibly-useful status applied specifically after subthalamic stimulation and dopamine-agonist withdrawal. These findings should not be generalized to every patient with apathy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] Pimavanserin improved PD psychosis in the placebo-controlled phase 3 trial without worsening motor function. The 2019 MDS review judged short-term efficacy sufficient for a clinically useful rating, while explicitly noting the limited controlled safety evidence beyond six weeks available to that review. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24183563/
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review scoped its positive piribedil apathy conclusion to patients after subthalamic nucleus stimulation and initial dopamine-agonist withdrawal; it rated rotigotine unlikely efficacious after a negative high-quality apathy trial, despite post hoc signals. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] In the 2024 OXYDOPA trial in parkinsonian central pain, neither prolonged-release oxycodone nor higher-dose levodopa demonstrated superiority over placebo. Adverse events leading to discontinuation were more frequent with oxycodone; the finding applies to this central-pain population. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38850081/ · keywords: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms
- [statement] NICE recommends considering clonazepam or melatonin for PD-related RBD after reviewing medication causes; the 2023 AASM guideline conditionally suggests clonazepam and specifically immediate-release melatonin for secondary RBD. These are conditional treatment options rather than proof that every formulation works. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] For secondary RBD, the AASM advises accounting for clonazepam-related sedation and imbalance, especially in older adults; reported adverse events include daytime sleepiness, dizziness and postural instability. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] Modafinil evidence in PD is mixed: MDS 2019 calls it possibly useful while retaining insufficient efficacy evidence, and one placebo-controlled trial found no significant improvement in either Epworth scores or objective sleep latency. Response should not be assumed. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] The cited sources note that clonazepam for RBD carries risks including morning sedation, gait imbalance or falls, cognitive adverse effects, and worsening sleep-disordered breathing; age and pre-existing imbalance affect selection and dosing. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] The 2023 AASM guideline conditionally supports transdermal rivastigmine for PD-associated RBD, based on one randomized trial; reported adverse effects include hypotension, asthenia, daytime sleepiness and nausea. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10071384/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] The LEAP trial authors conclude that levodopa combined with carbidopa had no disease-modifying effect in early Parkinson’s disease over 80 weeks. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30673543/
- [statement] The EMA Parkinson’s guideline states that for early untreated Parkinson’s disease the goal is to slow progression of motor symptoms by assessing change in UPDRS, or time to L-Dopa+/DA-agonists, with a trial duration probably up to 24 months. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease_en.pdf-0
- [statement] The same EMA questions-and-answers document states that, because L-dopa is increasingly given as initial treatment, the start of L-dopa therapy is no longer an optimal demarcation criterion between early and more advanced Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/questions-and-answers-additional-clarification-inclusion-criteria-guideline-clinical-investigation-medicinal-products-treatment-parkinsons-disease-revision-2_en.pdf
- [statement] AbbVie announced FDA approval of VYALEV, foscarbidopa and foslevodopa, for motor fluctuations in adults with advanced Parkinson’s disease; this claim records the sponsor’s announcement. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-10-17) — https://news.abbvie.com/2024-10-17-U-S-FDA-Approves-VYALEV-TM-foscarbidopa-and-foslevodopa-for-Adults-Living-with-Advanced-Parkinsons-Disease · keywords: Regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) for PD therapies
- [statement] AbbVie announced submission of a New Drug Application to FDA for tavapadon as a treatment for Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-26) — https://news.abbvie.com/2025-09-26-AbbVie-Submits-New-Drug-Application-to-U-S-FDA-for-Tavapadon-for-the-Treatment-of-Parkinsons-Disease · keywords: Regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) for PD therapies
- [statement] FDA’s novel-drug list records Juvmo, tavapadon, approved on 9/25/2026 for Parkinson’s disease in adults; AbbVie subsequently announced JUVMO approval on Sept. 28, 2026. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.fda.gov/drugs/novel-drug-approvals-fda/novel-drug-approvals-2026 · keywords: Regulatory pathways (FDA, EMA) for PD therapies

## Parkinson's disease-modification research: GLP-1 agonists, LRRK2, GBA1, anti-alpha-synuclein, mitophagy, neuroinflammation and lessons from failed trials
<a id="parkinson-s-disease-modification-research-glp-1-agonists-lrrk2-gba1-anti-alpha-synuclein-mitophagy-neuroinflammation-and-lessons-from-failed-trials"></a>

- [statement] The EJS ACT-PD consortium describes a multi-arm, multi-stage (MAMS) platform trial design that will start with one placebo and three treatment arms, each with 400 participants, with a primary endpoint at 3 years powered to detect a 30% reduction in rate of progression of MDS-UPDRS Part I and II summed scores, with ineffective arms closed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616524/
- [statement] Ahlskog and Uitti argue that interpretation of the ADAGIO rasagiline delayed-start trials is problematic because of divergent results with the 2 symptomatically beneficial doses and variability in UPDRS scores with active rasagiline that was twice the magnitude of the major finding. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2865777/
- [statement] A ClinicalTrials.gov-based analysis of Parkinson's disease drug trials registered between 2015–2024 reports 444 trials, of which 42% were in Phase 1, 46% in Phase 2 and 12% in Phase 3, with 63% evaluating symptomatic therapies and 37% testing disease-modifying therapies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13442941/
- [statement] Mari and Mestre describe a “valley of death” in Parkinson's disease modification populated by failures such as the various NET-PD trials, the ADAGIO trial, the more recent α-Synuclein immunotherapy trials and the Ven-glustat trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8920063/
- [statement] Isradipine evidence is split: the STEADY-PD III report concluded that isradipine did not slow clinical progression, while a re-analysis of STEADY-PD II data reports significantly smaller total and part 3 UPDRS scores with 10 mg/day ER isradipine than placebo at trial end, with post hoc adjustment for symptomatic therapy diminishing the statistical significance. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/
- [statement] In FAIRPARK-II (NCT02655315), a phase 2 trial in participants with newly diagnosed Parkinson's disease who had never received levodopa, the authors report that the mean MDS-UPDRS total score worsened by 15.6 points with deferiprone and 6.3 points with placebo (difference, 9.3 points; 95% confidence interval, 6.3 to 12.2; P<0.001) at 36 weeks, and the trial team's statement likewise reports greater deterioration with deferiprone than with placebo. (high confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2209254
- [statement] Reviewers report that disease-modification trials in neurodegenerative disorders have struggled to separate symptomatic effects of putative agents from disease modification, and that documenting a disease-modifying effect is difficult for a Parkinson's disease drug with symptomatic benefit. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/
- [statement] A systematic review that searched 1980–2015 included 128 RCTs (84 in AD, 44 in PD) and concluded that none of the included studies convincingly demonstrated disease-modification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/
- [statement] A PRISMA-compliant review of phase II and III disease-modifying trials (2020-2025) with at least one target-engagement biomarker included 26 trials (PD=19, MSA=4, DLB=3); the authors report that only 8/26 studies demonstrated both target engagement and statistically significant clinical benefit and that nine trials showed target engagement without clinical benefit. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42861702/
- [statement] SURE-PD3 (NCT02642393), a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of inosine in early Parkinson's disease, randomized 298 participants and closed early after a prespecified interim futility analysis; the authors report MDS-UPDRS progression of 11.1 points per year with inosine versus 9.9 with placebo (P =.18). (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34519802/
- [statement] STEADY-PD III (NCT02168842), a phase 3 trial that randomized 336 patients with early Parkinson's disease to isradipine 5 mg twice daily or placebo for 36 months, reported adjusted least-squares mean changes in total UPDRS of 2.99 versus 3.26 points (treatment effect —0.27; P = 0.85), and its authors conclude that isradipine did not slow clinical progression. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/
- [statement] In the SPARK phase 2 trial (NCT03318523) of cinpanemab in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report the trial was stopped after the week 72 interim analysis owing to lack of efficacy, with a week 52 change in MDS-UPDRS of 10.8 points in the control group versus 10.5, 11.3 and 10.9 points in the 250-mg, 1250-mg and 3500-mg groups. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35921450/
- [statement] The STEADY-PD III authors state that the isradipine dose may have been insufficient to engage the target calcium channels associated with neuroprotective effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/
- [statement] In the bemdaneprocel phase I trial, twelve patients were enrolled sequentially in a low-dose cohort of 0.9 million cells and a high-dose cohort of 2.7 million cells, and all of the participants received one year of immunosuppression. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-08845-y
- [statement] A review article on clinical trials in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease states that where GBA1 variants exert a toxic gain-of-function effect, gene therapy alone may not be sufficient, and that a strategy combining an antisense oligonucleotide with gene therapy to restore functional GBA1 may be required. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors
- [statement] The phase 1b trial NCT04167540 of AAV2-GDNF (AB-1005) enrolled 11 participants, 5 in the Mild Cohort and 6 in the Moderate Cohort, per the authors' abstract and the registry record. (medium confidence) — https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000206690 · keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors
- [statement] The authors of the AAV2-GAD sham-surgery trial report that at the 6-month endpoint the UPDRS score decreased by 8·1 points in the AAV2-GAD group and by 4·7 points in the sham group, and that the AAV2-GAD group showed a significantly greater improvement over the 6-month course of the study (RMANOVA, p=0·04). (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21419704/ · keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors
- [statement] A review describes the PROPEL study (NCT04127578) of AAV9-GBA1 (PR001/LY3884961) as a phase 1/2a study that aims to evaluate the safety and tolerability of PR001 in individuals with moderate to severe PD who carry at least one GBA1 mutation, with PR001 administered via intracisternal injection. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12126811/ · keywords: Gene therapy in PD: AAV-GDNF/AADC/GAD and GBA1 vectors
- [statement] Selected short-term cognitive-test gains should not be presented as proof of dementia prevention: the PD-MCI group-training study called for longitudinal testing, whereas COGTIPS found no long-term cognitive or cognitive-status conversion advantage. The studies used different populations and training protocols. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7721510/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] Protein redistribution means limiting protein at breakfast and lunch while shifting intake toward dinner. It may improve levodopa response in selected patients with motor fluctuations, but definitions, patient selection and treatment algorithms lack consensus and high-level evidence is limited. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-023-00541-w

- [statement] In an 8-week pilot randomized trial, 47 people were randomized to low-fat or ketogenic diets and 38 completed. Ketogenic participants improved more on MDS-UPDRS Part 1 nonmotor experiences, but there were no between-group differences in Parts 2–4; intermittent worsening of tremor or rigidity was the most common ketogenic adverse effect. These results do not establish motor superiority or long-term safety. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6175383/
- [statement] The ketogenic pilot reported exacerbated tremor or rigidity as the most common ketogenic-group adverse effect. - [statement] Wang and Xu propose that upstream PINK1/Parkin activation can become partly uncoupled from downstream mitochondrial clearance under Parkinson’s disease-relevant conditions; pathway activation therefore does not necessarily demonstrate completed mitophagy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-24) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13341507/
- [statement] The Mouton-Liger review describes excessive microglial activation in postmortem Parkinson’s disease brains as a feature of brain neuroinflammation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/
- [statement] Sulzer and colleagues report that α-synuclein-derived peptides act as antigenic epitopes driving helper and cytotoxic T cell responses in patients with Parkinson’s disease. (low confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/nature22815
- [statement] Within the MPTP mouse model, Brochard and colleagues attribute T cell-mediated dopaminergic toxicity predominantly to CD4+ T cells requiring FasL expression rather than IFNγ. (low confidence) — https://www.jci.org/articles/view/36470
- [statement] Mazzulli and colleagues report that functional loss of glucocerebrosidase compromises lysosomal protein degradation in primary cultures or human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3132082/
- [statement] The Mouton-Liger review describes mammalian-cell evidence that PINK1 and Parkin jointly regulate clearance of dysfunctional mitochondria through autophagy and lysosomal degradation, termed mitophagy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5410576/
- [statement] McWilliams and colleagues report that loss of Pink1 did not alter basal mitophagy in the mouse tissues examined apart from pancreatic islets; this limits extrapolation from depolarization-induced pathway activation to basal mitochondrial turnover. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5807059/
- [statement] Brochard and colleagues report attenuation of MPTP-induced dopaminergic cell death in mice lacking CD4. (low confidence) — https://www.jci.org/articles/view/36470
- [statement] Mirabegron results differ by study and endpoint: PaDoMi reported improved overactive-bladder symptom scores at Weeks 4 and 8 in a Parkinsonism population, whereas MAESTRO did not achieve its primary composite symptom endpoint when mirabegron was added to behavioral modification including pelvic floor exercises. These are differing study results, rather than proof of universal benefit or no benefit. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33389776/
- [statement] Macrogol has placebo-controlled evidence for PD constipation and was rated likely efficacious and possibly useful in the 2019 MDS review. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/
- [statement] In the placebo-controlled lubiprostone trial, short-term constipation improvement favored active treatment, while intermittent loose stools were the most common reported adverse event. These findings do not establish long-term comparative effectiveness. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22573627/
- [statement] Macrogol and lubiprostone have supportive PD constipation trial evidence, but this should be described with the limits of small, short studies. The 2019 MDS review classified both as likely efficacious and possibly useful; the 2018 constipation review cautioned against strong recommendations from the evidence then available. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856748/
- [statement] The rimabotulinumtoxinB trial describes neurological sialorrhea, including PD, as usually reflecting inefficient elimination of oral saliva rather than increased saliva production. (low confidence) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurol/articlepdf/10.1001/jamaneurol.2019.4565 · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] The SIAXI trial, which included adults with PD and other neurological conditions, found incobotulinumtoxinA 100 U improved salivary flow and patient global change versus placebo at week 4, with effects observed at week 16. NICE supports specialist consideration of botulinum toxin A for drooling. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30918101/ · keywords: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
- [statement] Rotigotine is not an established apathy treatment: the 2019 MDS review rated it unlikely efficacious, and a later placebo-controlled study in drug-naive PD also missed its apathy primary outcome. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/
- [statement] NICE NG71 says not to offer olanzapine for PD psychosis, and the 2019 MDS review rated it not efficacious with unacceptable risk. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations
- [statement] In a placebo-controlled trial of thirty people with PD-RBD, prolonged-release melatonin 4 mg did not reduce RBD events; the primary endpoint comparison was not significant (P = 0.92). This finding concerns that formulation and trial, rather than disproving all melatonin regimens. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31674060/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] A negative prolonged-release melatonin trial should not be presented as a test of immediate-release melatonin: in 30 PD patients, 4 mg prolonged-release melatonin over 8 weeks did not reduce RBD compared with placebo, while AASM separately conditionally recommends immediate-release melatonin and finds insufficient evidence for prolonged-release melatonin in secondary RBD. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7027846/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
- [statement] The 2019 MDS review rated melatonin and eszopiclone for PD insomnia as possibly useful despite insufficient efficacy evidence; these ratings should not be rewritten as established efficacy. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6916382/ · keywords: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness

## Parkinson's disease rehabilitation and adjunct therapies: exercise, physical, speech and occupational therapy, dance, music, acupuncture, cannabis and supplements
<a id="parkinson-s-disease-rehabilitation-and-adjunct-therapies-exercise-physical-speech-and-occupational-therapy-dance-music-acupuncture-cannabis-and-supplements"></a>

- [statement] Sources differ in how firmly they describe exercise as slowing PD progression: the Parkinson's Foundation exercise page and a physiotherapy review state progression-related benefits (slowed symptom progression, a potential neuroprotective effect, delayed disability), whereas the APTA guideline, a review by Crotty and Schwarzschild and the SPARX3 protocol describe whether exercise modifies disease progression as an open question. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.parkinson.org/living-with-parkinsons/treatment/exercise · keywords: Exercise and physical therapy in PD
- [statement] Two recent systematic reviews of singing in Parkinson's disease word their conclusions differently: Irons and Sheffield (23 studies, 540 participants; last search 3 April 2025) rate the certainty of the one RCT-based favourable outcome as very low and state that, due to insufficient high-quality evidence, they are unable to determine the effects of singing interventions, whereas Trinchillo and colleagues (twenty-six studies, 1057 patients; considerable heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis) conclude that singing is a promising adjunct therapy. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12645629/ · keywords: Music, art and creative therapies in PD
- [statement] A systematic review of active group-based performing arts interventions in Parkinson's disease (searches conducted in February 2020) included fifty-six studies reported in 67 publications with a total of 1531 people with PD; dance was studied most (38 studies), followed by 12 studies on singing, four on music therapy and two on theatrical interventions, and the authors state that no studies compared interventions from different performing arts modalities. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7547481/ · keywords: Music, art and creative therapies in PD
- [statement] Reviews and a patient-organisation page describe the creative-therapy evidence base in Parkinson's disease as limited by small samples and weak designs: Barnish and Barran list small sample sizes and the absence of control groups in over half of the included studies among the main methodological concerns, Irons and Sheffield report that most singing studies' methods were not rated highly due to small sample sizes, blinding and weak study design, and the American Parkinson Disease Association page states that most complementary therapies, which it lists as including singing, music therapy, dance therapy, theater and art therapy, have usually been studied only in small groups of people. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7547481/ · keywords: Music, art and creative therapies in PD
- [statement] On visual-art therapy in Parkinson's disease, an observational, prospective, open-label, exploratory study of eighteen patients reported improved Navon test, eye-tracking and UPDRS performance after twenty sessions of art therapy, whereas the authors of an art-therapy meta-analysis state that visual arts and painting represent a significant research gap whose direct therapeutic effects remain unexplored. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33526323/ · keywords: Music, art and creative therapies in PD
- [statement] In WATCH-PD, participants wore the smartwatch at home for seven days after each clinic visit and completed motor, speech and cognitive tasks on the smartphone every other week. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10108794/ · keywords: Digital biomarkers: wearables and remote monitoring in PD
- [statement] Nicotine has not demonstrated clinical benefit as a PD treatment: a randomized early-PD trial found that one year of transdermal nicotine did not slow progression, and a 2025 meta-analysis found no significant pooled short- or long-term motor improvement. The meta-analysis includes the trial and is corroborating synthesis rather than an independent replication. (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38320207/
- [statement] A small preliminary randomised trial enrolled 30 distressed care partners and compared 12–14 CBT sessions with no treatment; it reported greater improvement in psychological distress, strain and subjective burden, maintained over a further three-month follow-up. The authors called for larger studies and longer-term assessment. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1739584/ · keywords: Care partner support and caregiver burden in PD
- [statement] In a randomized trial of 72 people with PD and depression, a 10-session telephone CBT intervention added to usual care improved Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores by 6.53 points versus −0.27 with usual care; benefits persisted during six-month follow-up that included monthly CBT contacts. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7282876/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] Mindfulness-based yoga and meditation trials in mild-to-moderate PD suggest benefits for depressive symptoms compared with stretching and resistance exercise, but these programs and selected trial populations differ, so a single effect size should not be generalized across them. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6583059/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] The mindfulness-yoga trial reported greater anxiety, depression and health-related quality-of-life improvement than stretching/resistance exercise, with similar physical benefits. Yoga classes lasted 90 minutes versus 60 minutes for controls. Unblinded participants, convenience sampling and exclusion of severe motor limitations restrict attribution and generalization. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6583059/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] Gwak and Park’s 2026 anxiety meta-analysis reported a pooled benefit for psychological and mind–body interventions but rated overall evidence certainty very low. The prediction interval included no effect, and most comparisons used inactive controls. The mindfulness/mind–body subgroup interval included no effect; subgroup differences were not statistically established. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13685121/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] The PD-MCI group-training trial randomized 64 participants to six weeks of multidomain training or low-intensity physical activity; phonemic fluency improved significantly, but the overall executive-function interaction was only a statistical trend. The authors called for longitudinal studies before inferring slower cognitive decline. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7721510/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] In the mindfulness-yoga trial, 138 participants received eight weeks of yoga or stretching/resistance exercise; the yoga program reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms and improved health-related quality of life, while motor dysfunction and mobility benefits were described as comparable to exercise. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6583059/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] In the 68-participant mindfulness-meditation trial, both meditation and exercise groups improved on cognitive performance immediately after treatment; meditation was not shown to provide a superior cognitive benefit. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9862216/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] Cognitive-training findings in PD are task-specific and inconsistent: one PD-MCI trial favored training on phonemic fluency, whereas a larger computerized-training trial found no benefit on its primary planning-accuracy outcome and no group differences at follow-up. These results do not establish broad or durable cognitive improvement. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7721510/ · keywords: CBT, mindfulness and cognitive training in PD
- [statement] The APTA guideline strongly recommends physical-therapist-delivered balance training to improve postural control, balance, gait, mobility, balance confidence and quality of life. These outcomes should be distinguished from a demonstrated reduction in falls. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9046970/ · keywords: Fall prevention, home safety and mobility aids in PD
- [statement] In a 2014 randomized trial of 191 people with PD and daily-activity difficulties, a 10-week home occupational-therapy intervention improved self-perceived daily activity performance at 3 months compared with usual care without occupational therapy; the endpoint does not establish disease modification. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24726066/ · keywords: Living well with PD: driving, work, travel and daily living
- [statement] A 2022 review of multidisciplinary rehabilitation versus conventional physiotherapy included 6 studies and 1260 participants and found no statistically significant difference in functionality, disability, or quality of life. This rehabilitation comparison should not be treated as testing every integrated specialist-care model. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8901313/ · keywords: Multidisciplinary care models and telemedicine in PD
- [statement] A 2024 randomized study of fifty participants evaluated additional nurse, neurologist, and occupational-therapist telemedicine alongside office visits, reporting less frailty and improved quality of life. This is evidence for that small hybrid program, rather than proof that any video visit improves outcomes. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39586130/ · keywords: Multidisciplinary care models and telemedicine in PD
